key_insight: A transverse-field Ising model with a globally controlled, non-monotonic time-dependent field can simulate arbitrary quantum circuits with only polynomial overhead, making it computationally equivalent to the gate model in principle.
engineering_relevance: This result broadens the theoretical foundation for analog quantum computing and quantum annealing platforms by showing they can, under global control, support universal computation rather than only optimization.
method: Constructs a simulation mapping from arbitrary gate-model circuits to the global-field Ising dynamics.
Uses a non-monotonic time-dependent transverse field as the global control resource.
Builds on the Cesa-Pichler global-control framework and proves polynomial scaling in time, qubits, and energy.
evidence_signal: The paper’s evidence is a theoretical construction and complexity analysis, establishing polynomial overhead rather than reporting experimental data or benchmark measurements.
watch_item: The polynomial overheads are described as very large, so practical implementation on near-term hardware may be far from feasible.
paper_title: Polynomial equivalence of the global transverse-field Ising model and the gate model of quantum computation
